chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from al-Ahwal, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), regarding:

A man who fasted a month as the expiation for Dhahir, then found a slave to free, he said: 'He frees her and does not count the fasting.' The view in this narration is that we interpret it as a type of recommended act (istihbab) rather than obligatory (farḍ) and compulsory (ijbar).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one fasts for Dhahir expiation and then finds a slave to free?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to clarify the hierarchy of expiation options for Dhahir, where freeing a slave takes precedence over fasting. The juristic interpretation that the fasting is merely recommended (istihbab) rather than obligatory (ijbar) highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh when the primary condition (finding a slave) is met after partial fulfillment of the secondary condition. This ruling underscores the principle that the most capable form of expiation supersedes the lesser one once the means become available.
